post_title: How many turkey poults will USDA NASS report as net placed in the United States during October 2026?

question.title: How many turkey poults will USDA NASS report as net placed in the United States during October 2026?
question.description:
USDA NASS publishes the monthly Turkey Hatchery report (usually between the 12th and 14th of each month at 3:00 p.m. ET), based on a survey of about 30 hatcheries in 17 states. It reports three things: turkey eggs in incubators on the first of the month, poults hatched during the month, and net poults placed during the month. Net poult placements are the poults delivered to grow-out farms, and October is seasonally one of the two largest months of the year, because poults placed in October reach market weight around the Thanksgiving-to-New Year window.

Status quo (report released October 13, 2026): turkey eggs in incubators on October 1, 2026 totaled 26,695 thousand, up 8% from 24,814 thousand on September 1 and up 2% from a year earlier; poults hatched in September 2026 totaled 21,122 thousand, up 2% year over year but down 3% from August's 21,873 thousand; and net poults placed in September 2026 totaled 19,571 thousand - up 2% from September 2025's 19,096 thousand but down 8% from August 2026's 21,164 thousand. For comparison, net poult placements were 21,284 thousand in October 2025 and 18,482 thousand in November 2025, and the September-to-October step in 2025 was about +11%. NASS's own reliability note puts the root mean square error for net poult placements at 4.2% (90% confidence interval plus or minus 7.1%), so month-to-month misses of several hundred thousand poults are normal.

The H5N1 backdrop matters for October. The autumn 2026 wave of highly pathogenic H5N1 has hit the turkey belt hard: USDA APHIS data summarized on October 30, 2026 show 11 commercial flocks confirmed in the previous 30 days, including commercial turkey operations of 60,600 birds in Dickey County, North Dakota (October 21), 57,500 birds in Roseau County, Minnesota and 13,500 in Barron County, Wisconsin (October 22), and 44,400 birds in Sac County, Iowa (October 28). Minnesota has now lost 20 commercial flocks in 2026 and Wisconsin six. Depopulated grow-out barns, control-area movement restrictions and delayed placements can push the national figure either way: affected producers defer placements, while unaffected producers may add poults to fill holiday demand.

The October 2026 figures will not exist publicly until the November 13 release, so the number is fully unknown as forecasting opens.

question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the October 2026 net poult placements figure published in USDA NASS's [Turkey Hatchery](https://esmis.nal.usda.gov/publication/turkey-hatchery) report scheduled for release at 3:00 p.m. ET on November 13, 2026. Use the value for October 2026 in the report's net poult placements table for the United States (total all breeds), which NASS publishes in thousands of poults; for example, a reported figure of 19,571 thousand poults resolves as 19,571. The figure as first published in that report governs, and revisions published in later NASS reports do not change the resolution. If the report does not include an October 2026 placement estimate, resolution waits for the next NASS report that contains it.
question.fine_print:
- Use NASS's published estimate as-is, including all breeds; do not adjust it for exports, deaths in transit, or any other factor.
- The other figures in the same report (turkey eggs in incubators on November 1, poults hatched in October, percentages of a year earlier) are context only and are not the resolution value.
- Only the October 2026 placement figure counts, not the September or November estimates or the November 1 eggs-in-incubators value.
